chunks: From him, from Abu Abdillah, from Mansur ibn Abbas, from Ismail ibn Sahl al-Katib, from Abu Talib al-Ghanawi, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Allah forbade the women (from entering the mosque) upon Ali (peace be upon him) as long as Fatimah (peace be upon her) was alive. I said, 'How?' He said, 'Because she is pure (al-Tahira) and does not menstruate.'
ai.seo_question: Why were women forbidden from entering the mosque according to this hadith from Imam Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the unique ritual status of Fatimah al-Zahra (SA), linking her perpetual purity (Tahara) to a specific legal prohibition regarding women's access to mosques during her lifetime. Shia scholars interpret this not merely as a physical absence of menstruation, but as a sign of her exceptional spiritual and ritual purity, distinguishing her from other women in the context of mosque entry rules.
